title: Universally tensor-flat free dg modules on graded sheaves of sets
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ commutative, and use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and cohomology of cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf of associative unital graded $\mathcal O$-algebras with an $\mathcal O$-linear differential of degree one, $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(b)$. A right dg $\mathcal A$-module is a graded sheaf with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^{|m|}m\,d(a)$; left modules have $d(am)=d(a)m+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(m)$. Tensor products mean sheafifications of the balanced graded tensor products, with direct-sum total grading and $d(p\otimes n)=dp\otimes n+(-1)^{|p|}p\otimes dn$. A quasi-isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all underlying cohomology sheaves. Let $\mathcal S$ be a sheaf of sets with a degree map $\mathcal S\to\underline{\mathbf Z}$. Write $F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S)$ for the right graded $\mathcal A$-module whose degree $n$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of
$$U\longmapsto\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbf Z}\ \bigoplus_{s\in\mathcal S_k(U)}s\mathcal A^{n-k}(U),$$
where $\mathcal S_k$ is the fibre of the degree map over the constant integer $k$, and $|s|=k$ for $s\in\mathcal S_k(U)$. The right action is multiplication on the coefficient. Endow it with $d(s)=0$ and $d(sa)=(-1)^{|s|}s\,d(a)$. Then $F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S)\otimes_{\mathcal A}-$ is exact on graded left modules, and $F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S)\otimes_{\mathcal A}N$ is acyclic whenever the left dg module $N$ is acyclic. For every small ringed site $(\mathcal C^{\prime},\mathcal O^{\prime})$ with $\mathcal O^{\prime}$ commutative, every ringed-topos morphism $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C^{\prime}),\mathcal O^{\prime})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], every sheaf dg $\mathcal O^{\prime}$-algebra $\mathcal A^{\prime}$, and every dg algebra map $f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ there is a natural isomorphism of dg modules
$$f^{-1}F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S)\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal A}\mathcal A'\cong F_{\mathcal A'}(f^{-1}\mathcal S),$$
which sends a pulled-back generator to the corresponding generator. In particular the two tensor assertions hold after every such base change. No boundedness, enough-points, or graded-commutativity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0FSG (lemma-free-graded-module-good), with construction in remark-sheaf-graded-sets, Tag 0FSF. Right-module convention; sheafification is taken over homogeneous local generators.

proof.text: Put $T_{\mathcal S}(M)^n=(U\mapsto\bigoplus_k\bigoplus_{s\in\mathcal S_k(U)}M^{n-k}(U))^\#$ for a graded module sheaf $M$, with restrictions summing coefficients when labels restrict to the same label. We may compute underlying sheafifications in abelian groups. By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] and [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection], applied to the sheafification unit (whose sheafification is an isomorphism by its universal property), every section is locally a finite sum, and equality of two such sums in the associated sheaf holds locally already in the presheaf. Thus one may refine a cover before comparing coefficients. These assertions use covering sieves and transitivity, not points or fibre products in the site.

source.place: Tag 0FSF, remark-sheaf-graded-sets, construction by sheafification; local interpretation of the sums in Tag 0FSG

proof.text: The prescribed differential respects restrictions. For $|s|=k$, $|a|=j$, $d^2(sa)=(-1)^{2k}s\,d^2a=0$, and $d(sab)=(-1)^ks\,d(a)b+(-1)^{k+j}sa\,d(b)$, the required right-module rule. Define $F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S)\otimes_{\mathcal A}M\to T_{\mathcal S}(M)$ by $(sa)\otimes m\mapsto s(am)$, with inverse $s m\mapsto s\otimes m$. Balanced relations identify the two composites with the identity. These formulas extend through the degreewise sheafifications by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension]; finite sums of total degrees give the graded maps. For a dg $M$ the differential on the right is $D(sm)=(-1)^ks\,dm$: on $(sa)\otimes m$ both differential formulas give $(-1)^ks(d(a)m)+(-1)^{k+j}s(a\,dm)$. The identification is natural and is an isomorphism of underlying complexes.

source.place: Tag 0FSG, lemma-free-graded-module-good, first displayed tensor identification; Tag 0FSF, differential convention

proof.text: We prove exactness of $T_{\mathcal S}$ degreewise. Kernels of sheaf maps are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. For an exact sequence $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$, take a finite local representative $\sum s m_s$ of a section of $T_{\mathcal S}(M_2)$ whose image is zero. Refine until its image is zero as a presheaf sum, and combine equal restricted labels. Each resulting coefficient belongs to the kernel in $M_2$, so comes uniquely from $M_1$. If a representative from $T_{\mathcal S}(M_1)$ maps to zero, the same refinement and coefficient argument makes it zero, proving injectivity. Finally, each of the finitely many coefficients of a representative in $T_{\mathcal S}(M_3)$ lifts locally to $M_2$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective]. Repeated pullback of covering sieves and transitivity give one refinement for all coefficients. Hence the map onto $T_{\mathcal S}(M_3)$ is locally surjective and therefore epic by the same node. This proves the graded tensor exactness through step 2.

source.place: Tag 0FSG, first paragraph: exactness of the functor on graded sheaves; expanded coefficient lifting argument

proof.text: Suppose $N$ is acyclic and let $z$ be a local cycle of degree $n$ in $T_{\mathcal S}(N)$. By step 1 it is locally represented by a finite sum $\sum s n_s$. Refine until $Dz=0$ already in the presheaf and combine equal restricted labels. Then $d n_s=0$ for each surviving label $s$ of degree $k$. Acyclicity says $d:N^{n-k-1}\to Z^{n-k}(N)$ is epic; by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] and a common finite refinement choose $b_s$ with $db_s=n_s$. Now $D(\sum_s(-1)^k s b_s)=\sum_s s n_s=z$. Thus the map from degree $n-1$ onto degree-$n$ cycles is locally surjective, hence epic by the cited node. Kernels are computed sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], so all cohomology sheaves vanish. This argument uses finite support in each representative even when generators and complexes have unbounded degrees.

source.place: Tag 0FSG, cohomology calculation and acyclic tensor assertion; local cycle-boundary version

proof.text: Write $B_k=\mathcal O[\mathcal S_k]$. The given construction has underlying graded module $F^n=\bigoplus_k B_k\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal A^{n-k}$: the mutually inverse maps on local sums are $[s]\otimes a\mapsto sa$ and $sa\mapsto[s]\otimes a$, extended by the bilinear sheafification node and the universal property of module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. On module sheaves $f^{-1}$ preserves direct sums: by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] with $S=f^{-1}\mathcal O$ and $c$ the identity, $M\mapsto f^{-1}\mathcal O\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O}f^{-1}M\cong f^{-1}M$ is left adjoint to direct image of $f^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules, so $\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}\bigoplus_iM_i,H)$ is the product of the $\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}M_i,H)$. Finite-limit preservation identifies $f^{-1}\mathcal S_k$ with $(f^{-1}\mathcal S)_k$; here $f^{-1}\underline{\mathbf Z}=\underline{\mathbf Z}$ since the constant integer sheaf is the coproduct of terminal sheaves and $f^{-1}$ preserves both. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-free-module] with the commutative ring $\mathcal O$ and each $\mathcal S_k$, and [lem-pur-independent-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] to $B_k\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal A^j$. We obtain $f^{-1}F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S)\cong F_{f^{-1}\mathcal A}(f^{-1}\mathcal S)$, taking pulled-back $sa$ to the corresponding $sa$. It respects the right action because the action is coefficient multiplication, and respects $d(sa)=(-1)^ks\,da$ because both comparisons preserve the generating pure tensors. No commutativity of $\mathcal A$ is used: the cited tensor comparison is over $\mathcal O$.

source.place: Tag 0FSG, final paragraph: inverse image of the free module; decomposed into free commutative-coefficient pieces

proof.text: Put $\mathcal B=f^{-1}\mathcal A$, $E=f^{-1}\mathcal S$, and let $\varphi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A'$ be the supplied map. Scalar extension gives the isomorphism $F_{\mathcal B}(E)\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A'\to F_{\mathcal A'}(E)$, $(sb)\otimes a'\mapsto s\varphi(b)a'$, with inverse $sa'\mapsto(s1)\otimes a'$. The balanced relation gives both inverse identities. The sheafified maps exist by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] over the constant ring $\mathbf Z$ (all formulas are additive in each variable, so no linearity of $\varphi$ over $f^{-1}\mathcal O$ is needed), and the inverse by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For $|s|=k$, $|b|=j$, the differential of either formula is $(-1)^ks\varphi(db)a'+(-1)^{k+j}s\varphi(b)da'$. Thus this is a dg isomorphism. Compose with step 5. The formula sends a pulled-back generator to $s1$, and commuting with maps of generators, dg coefficients and modules follows by substituting their images in this same formula. Applying steps 2--4 on the target site to $\mathcal A'$ and $E$ gives the two tensor assertions after every stated base change.

source.place: Tag 0FSG, final displayed base-change equality and conclusion
